report_name: German Drone Maker Quantum Systems Hit by Cyberattack

threat_actors.name: Unattributed Actors
threat_actors.description: The unidentified hostile actors responsible for the October 2026 supply chain attack against Quantum Systems.

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Software Supply Chain
attack_patterns.description: The attack on Quantum Systems was a potential software supply chain attack, aiming to distribute a malicious software update by compromising the software distribution infrastructure.

attack_patterns.name: Code Signing
attack_patterns.description: Attackers would need to sign a malicious update with the vendor's authentic code-signing certificate to make it appear legitimate to customers.

attack_patterns.name: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
attack_patterns.description: A malicious payload would be disguised as a legitimate software update from Quantum Systems to deceive customers into installing it.

tools.name: signtool.exe
tools.description: The signtool.exe utility was identified as a relevant observable, likely to be used by attackers to sign a trojanized software update with a compromised code-signing certificate.

identities.name: Quantum Systems
identities.description: A German defense company specializing in reconnaissance and interceptor drones that was the target of a cyberattack in October 2026.

identities.name: MAD (Military Counterintelligence Service)
identities.description: German military counterintelligence agency investigating the cyberattack on Quantum Systems.

identities.name: BfV (Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution)
identities.description: German federal agency investigating the cyberattack on Quantum Systems.

identities.name: BSI (Federal Office for Information Security)
identities.description: German federal agency for information security investigating the cyberattack on Quantum Systems.

infrastructure.name: Software Distribution Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: The attackers targeted Quantum Systems' software distribution infrastructure, such as an update server, to potentially push malicious code disguised as a legitimate software update.

indicators.name: Suspicious Code Signing Activity
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Code Signing Activity
id: 2b8c3d1e-9f0a-4b1c-8d2e-5f6a7b8c9d0e
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of signtool.exe to sign files, which could indicate a software supply chain compromise attempt where attackers sign malicious code with a compromised certificate.
references:
  - https://securityaffairs.com/203085/cyber-crime/german-military-grounds-quantum-systems-drones-following-reported-cyberattack.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-16
tags:
  - attack.t1553.002
  - attack.defense_evasion
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\signtool.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'sign'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of signtool.exe with the 'sign' command, a TTP for legitimizing malicious code in a supply chain attack.
